title: Lighthouse retail — data sampling & fallback call notes
content:
Call date: 2026-02-19
Attendees: Maya (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood deploy eng), Priya (Lighthouse Sr Eng), Samir (Lighthouse infra), Monica (Lighthouse PM, joined 15m)

Quick summary:
- Lighthouse (regional retail chain) exploring a hybrid deployment: private (VPC) control plane with a lightweight on-prem inference tier for store-level assistants.
- Primary asks: sub-100ms local latency for cashier-facing autocomplete and inventory lookup; strict PII isolation (no persistent tokenization across stores); predictable monthly committed capacity for peak hours (weekend promos).
- They are worried about model drift and want an easy rollback / canary experience. Also cost sensitivity on per-token spend for hosted fallback.

Notes and clarifications captured during the call (raw):
- Priya: "We have inconsistent network out of some stores; can't rely on cloud for 100% of requests."
- Samir: "Edge boxes are small: 1xA10G in most stores; some stores can take 2xA10G. Budget limits us from heavy infra changes."
- Monica: "Compliance: customer contact transcripts must not be persisted outside the VPC; need audit logs for any model invocation that touches PII."
- Diego: "We want to start with a smaller LM (7B) and fallback to hosted 13B only when quality is unacceptable — but we need automated, observable fallbacks so ops don't get paged constantly."

Inferred requirements (prioritize):
1) Local inference SLO: p95 tail <= 120ms for 128-token responses for autocomplete flows. (We should validate what they mean by tokens here — they might mean characters).
2) Data residency: store-level data must remain in-store or in customer VPC; telemetry metadata can be aggregated but must not contain user utterances.
3) Fallback policy: first try on-prem 7B; if confidence < threshold OR latency > SLO OR kv-cache miss for prefix, route to hosted 13B in region with egress logging. Must annotate logs with masked PII flag.
4) Canary + rollback: ability to route X% traffic to new model binary and automatic rollback on quality regressions (measured by prompt QA set and production signal).
5) Cost cap: monthly hosted fallback spend <= $12k initial pilot; we need per-route cost estimates.

Gotchas / red flags (actionable):
- On-prem hardware: A10G quantization characteristics -> need to check if 7B q4f16 / q8 configurations hit the latency target. If not, may require additional batching (risk to latency) or using a trimmed context window.
- Network egress: some stores have asymmetric NAT which breaks persistent websocket streaming; fallback must support both streaming and non-streaming REST.
- Security: KMS integration — they use Azure Key Vault. We need to confirm compatibility for Private control plane secrets and whether HSM is required for enterprise contract.
- Logging/PII: They asked for full audit trails but compliance says transcripts can't leave VPC. We may need to ship structured telemetry (hashes + event types) instead of raw text. Confirm exact fields Lighthouse legal will accept.
- Observability: They asked for per-model token-level cost breakdown. Our console has that, but verify retention windows and whether they need SAML access for a Lighthouse admin.

Initial technical approach (sketch):
- Private control plane in Lighthouse VPC (managed CP components) + small on-prem agents in stores (k3s+pod for runtime).
- Deploy Redwood runtime as an inference pod: 7B quantized variant tuned for A10G. Runtime configured with: small prefix cache (store catalog prefixes), dynamic batching disabled for autocomplete route, max_seq_length 128, response timeout 300ms.
- Router policy: local-first; health checks with active latency probe and confidence probe (LLM internal score -> patched calibrator). If probe fails, route to hosted 13B in us-west-2 (closest region) via secure peering/egress path.
- Fallback masking: when routing to hosted, redact PII (apply deterministic token replacement) before egress; include redaction metadata in audit log.

Prompt examples they shared (copied verbatim):
- "SKU lookup for cashier: 'price of SKU 234-81 in store 004?'"
- "Suggest 3 short responses to customer about returns policy for items without receipt"
We should prepare a small prompt-suite to measure quality delta between 7B on-device and hosted 13B.

Open questions (to resolve before next sync):
- Which fields are considered PII by Lighthouse legal? (email, phone, loyalty id, billing address?) Need checklist from their compliance team.
- Can we run a small benchmark image to test q4f16 latency on their exact A10G driver/kernel? Need SSH access to one test box or provide a micro-AMI they can run.
- Are there any egress inspection appliances in their WAN path that would prevent TLS to hosted region?
- Who will own the rollout gate in Lighthouse org for canary rollback? (Monica? Ops?) Need single point of contact for runbook triggers.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Maya: draft pilot architecture diagram + condensed runbook for canary rollback (ETA 2026-02-25).
- Diego: spin up local perf test harness for 7B q4f16 config and share scripts; ask infra team for sample SSH to test store (ETA 2026-02-27).
- Priya: send compliance contact details and PII definition (ETA 2026-02-23).
- Samir: confirm store hardware inventory (which stores have 2xA10G) and current OS/kernel (ETA 2026-02-24).
- Monica: estimate expected fallback traffic % during peak promo (ballpark) and confirm budget cap formally (ETA 2026-02-26).

Notes-to-self / talking points for next call:
- Emphasize that fallback == quality safety net, not primary reliability strategy. If local boxes are frequently failing, they should consider small reserved dedicated capacity for fallback (predictable spend).
- Bring up Optimize suggestions: quantization profiles + small KV cache for SKU prefixes can dramatically reduce token work. Prepare an example that shows token-cost delta with and without prefix caching for 10 common queries.
- Prepare sample SAML admin flow for console access and show token-level cost dashboards in 10-minute walkthrough.

Mock timeline for pilot (rough):
Week 0: mutual NDA signed + access to test box
Week 1: small perf benchmarks on on-prem config + iterate quantization variant
Week 2: prototype deploy in 3 pilot stores, local routing + hosted fallback enabled, run daily evals
Week 3-4: expand to 15 stores, observe fallback rate and cost; tune thresholds

Alternate options if latency targets fail:
- Option A: keep 7B local, but only use for autosuggest (short responses) and route any longer generative tasks to hosted 13B always (reduces local compute demands).
- Option B: use smaller context + aggressive prefix cache and accept slightly lower context length (96 tokens) to meet p95 latency.
- Option C: suggest Lighthouse upgrade path: 2xA10G in high-traffic stores for full-feature parity.

Misc scratch notes (non-client-facing):
- Investigate q8_0 vs q4f16 perf on A10G (benchmarks vary widely in upstream tests).
- Check if we can expose a lightweight 'masked-audit' blob that stores hashes + redaction map for 90 days in CP logs (legal might accept hashed text for debugging).

Next sync: propose 2026-03-03 10:00 PST (Monica prefers mornings).

-- End of notes --

(These are working notes — will convert into formal runbook & pilot proposal once we validate perf data.)
